findings.title: Delete-cache mutation never refreshes the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it has no `onSettled` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and the "Delete cached data" item are rendered from that query, and the query is created with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. If the parent does not pass `onChanged`, the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" time and a delete action for a cache that no longer exists. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in the mutation itself instead of relying on the caller.

findings.title: Plain Error thrown for not-found or unauthorized credential
findings.body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws a bare `Error`. tRPC turns that into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), which is logged as a server fault. It should throw a `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`. The input schema is also defined inline in `_router.tsx` as `z.number()` rather than in a `.schema.ts` file like the sibling procedures. It also does not require an integer.

findings.title: Migration header is wrong, and legacy rows get a misleading timestamp
findings.body: The header comment says the column is added "without a default value", but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. The comment is stale, auto-generated text and contradicts the migration. Because of the default, every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`. The UI will show "Last updated: <migration time>" for caches that may be much older, so the displayed freshness is inaccurate until each row is next upserted.

findings.title: Extra write to every SelectedCalendar row on each cache refresh, with no consumer
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `updateMany({ where: { credentialId } }, data: {})` after every cache refresh. That function runs from the Google webhook path and from `unwatchCalendar`. This adds a write against all of a credential's SelectedCalendar rows (user-level and event-type-level) on every webhook purely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The PR notes say the frontend does not read that field and uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. The write is wasted load and contention on a hot table. It also relies on Prisma bumping `@updatedAt` for an empty `data` object. Remove it.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The cache time is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's locale and time-format preference even though the surrounding string is translated with `t()`. Non-US users see US-style dates, for example M/D/YY. Use the active locale (for example `i18n.language`) or the app's date utilities.

findings.title: Unrelated dev script with macOS-only sed and wrong exit code
findings.body: This tunnel script has nothing to do with the cache feature. `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux) it treats `''` as the script and fails, so the env file is never updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the current working directory. `cleanup` always `exit 0`, including the failure paths at the rate-limit check and when no URL could be extracted. When reusing an existing tmole, the log file may not exist, so URL extraction silently returns nothing. It should be removed from this PR or fixed.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not declared in this package's dependencies or devDependencies. `npx` will download it on demand, so versions are unpinned and offline or CI use can fail. This change is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature.

findings.title: No tests for the new handler, repository method, or dropdown logic
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive mutation with an ownership check (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new `groupBy` query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), the `cacheUpdatedAt` enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and conditional dropdown rendering. None of them has a test. Ownership enforcement (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the credential-to-cache mapping should be covered.
